scope: Chodosh, Irie and Zahl report narratives and selected atomic branches. Definitions and elementary deductions are expanded; deep cited inputs, announced results, conditional theorems and deferred proofs remain distinguished.
source_method: Published SIAM full texts read in full, with versioned arXiv cross-checks and selected primary-paper passages as specified in the per-report packets. CC BY 4.0 attribution appears on each reference page.

reports.speaker: Otis Chodosh
reports.title: Minimal Surfaces and Comparison Geometry
reports.license: CC BY 4.0; copyright International Mathematical Union; publisher license checked on the official full-text page
reports.question: 怎样利用稳定极小超曲面与 μ 气泡，将局部曲率下界转化为流形的拓扑障碍、宽度限制和欧氏刚性？
reports.reading_scope: Read the official published full text, sections 1–14, including theorem hypotheses and proof sketches. Checked selected bibliography entries for theorem locations. Consulted arXiv v1 for version identity, not as a substitute for the published text. Read the sign conventions, Theorem 1.3, Lemma 2.2, Lemma 5.2 and Proposition 5.4 in Chodosh's December 5, 2021 Math 258 notes.

proof_scope.2G03: Full normal-variation computation, including metric derivative, normal derivative, Hessian term, curvature contraction and integration by parts.
proof_scope.2G05: Gauss equation derived from the tangential/normal connection decomposition, then doubly traced.
proof_scope.2G06: Gauss–Bonnet is cited; triangulation describes its derivation but is not labelled a complete proof.
proof_scope.2G07: Full deduction from the stability inequality and cited Gauss–Bonnet and surface classification.
proof_scope.2G08: Existence and regularity of the integral homology minimizer are cited; stability of each smooth component is deduced.
proof_scope.2G09: Full contradiction using a retracted nonzero torus class, the cited minimizer theorem, stable-surface topology and the Hurewicz image.
proof_scope.2G0B: Full positive-function quadratic-form identity by expansion and integration by parts.
proof_scope.2G0C: Full deduction using the cited existence of a positive first eigenfunction and the cited conformal scalar-curvature transformation formula.
proof_scope.2G0D: Both the lower bound and sharpness of the hyperbolic spectral bottom are proved; the rescaled counterexample uses a strictly greater than four.
proof_scope.2G0F: Full weighted second-variation computation and the three-dimensional curvature inequality.
proof_scope.2G0G: The sharp torical-band theorem is cited. The displayed cotangent barrier and its potential identity are verified directly; they are not presented as the complete width proof.
proof_scope.2G0K: The three-dimensional identity and the sum over orthonormal pairs are direct contractions.
proof_scope.2G0L: Full deduction of the spectral Ricci inequality from the Gauss equation and stability.
proof_scope.2G0M: Full graph-area Euler–Lagrange computation and equivalence with arbitrary compactly supported normal variations.
proof_scope.2G0N: Full calibration/Stokes proof for comparison surfaces whose difference bounds a compact piecewise-smooth oriented chain in the cylinder.
proof_scope.2G0O: Stable Bernstein is cited with intrinsic dimension at most five; its method is described without claiming a complete proof.
proof_scope.2G0P: Generic regularity in ambient dimension at most eleven is cited, distinguished from unconditional regularity in ambient dimension at most seven.
proof_scope.2G0Q: The spectral diameter theorem is cited; normalization of an arbitrary positive lower bound is calculated.
proof_scope.2G0R: Positive first eigenfunction existence is cited. One-dimensionality of the lowest eigenspace is proved using 2G0B.

deferred: Full geometric-measure-theory construction, compactness and regularity of codimension-one minimizers.
Full proof of Gauss–Bonnet and the elliptic analytic inputs to positive first eigenfunction existence.
Derivation of the conformal scalar-curvature transformation formula.
All-dimensional torus obstruction and its full iterative homological descent.
Theorem 7.2 localization, which needs careful dimensional and regularity assumptions beyond the condensed source statement.
Full mu-bubble existence, barrier regularization and exclusion of equality in the torical-band theorem.
Complete proofs of four- and five-dimensional aspherical obstructions, slice-and-dice decompositions, cover-width bounds and Corollary 9.4.
Section 10 noncompact and positive-mass branches; Section 11 Dirac and surgery comparisons.
Bi-Ricci diameter and spectral Bishop–Gromov theorems and their full proofs.
Complete stable Bernstein and generic-regularity proofs, including tangent cones and quantitative separation estimates.
The unresolved cases are reported as questions posed in the published report, not as independently refreshed claims about the research frontier.

reports.speaker: Kei Irie
reports.title: Strong Closing Lemmas in Hamiltonian Dynamics
reports.copyright: 2026 International Mathematical Union; published by SIAM
reports.question: 任意指定的同号局部扰动为何能迫使周期轨道或极小超曲面进入扰动区域，谱增长又在哪些维数和假设下足以证明这一点？
reports.reading_scope: Read the entire published report, sections 1–8 and references. Checked quantifiers, dimensions, rationality, perturbation composition, genus-limit order, announcement status, and conditional orbifold assumptions. Section 8 is integrated in 2H0P–2H0S and linked to the Chodosh branch.

proof_scope.2H04: Positive lower period bound and closedness of the finite-sum action spectrum proved; its nullity is cited from Irie Lemma 4.1, not inferred from arbitrary sums of null sets.
proof_scope.2H05: C0 continuity deduced from monotonicity and conformality; existence of ECH spectral selectors is cited.
proof_scope.2H07: Strong closing derived from ECH class existence, spectral axioms, null spectrum and the Weyl law; these deep inputs are cited, not reconstructed.
proof_scope.2H08: Negative perturbations proved by applying the three-dimensional theorem at the endpoint form and reversing the parameter.
proof_scope.2H09: Cotangent Hamilton equations, geodesic projection and the conformal factor one-half derived; the three-dimensional strong closing theorem is applied.
proof_scope.2H0C: Rationality of Hamiltonian surface maps proved by an explicit mapping-torus trivialization; the PFH closing theorem is cited.
proof_scope.2H0D: Reeb rotation formula, common-period criterion and the n-simple-orbit statement for pairwise irrational axis ratios proved directly.
proof_scope.2H0F: Simultaneous rational approximation and radial pullback explicitly prove the Hofer near-periodic estimate.
proof_scope.2H0I: The endpoint theorem is cited; conjugacy of left/right composition and the implication to strong closing are proved.
proof_scope.2H0J: Generic equidistribution is cited; density and normalized time-measure consequences are proved.
proof_scope.2H0L: Small-ball capacity inequality and telescoping small-gap implication proved using cited elementary-capacity properties and ball normalization.
proof_scope.2H0O: Local Darboux proof includes a radial primitive, the Moser vector field, local flow control, and coordinate verification of Cartan and pullback differentiation.
proof_scope.2H0P: Definitions of flat boundaries, k-sweepouts and widths recalled; Almgren topology, finiteness, min-max existence and smooth realization are cited inputs.
proof_scope.2H0Q: Bilinear-metric scaling, comparison bounds, C0 continuity and strict conformal volume growth proved; the volume-spectrum Weyl law is cited.
proof_scope.2H0R: The local perturbation conclusion is deduced from cited smooth min-max realization, bumpy-metric countability (now linked to 2H0S) and the Weyl law. The ambient range 3–7 and bumpy base metric remain explicit.
proof_scope.2H0S: Jacobi-kernel nondegeneracy and bumpy metrics defined separately. White genericity and Sharp bounded-area/index finiteness cited via Irie–Marques–Neves Proposition 3.1; countability follows by taking a countable union. Neither analytic theorem is claimed proved locally.

deferred: ECH and PFH analytic constructions, their cobordism maps, Weyl asymptotics and existence of suitable homology classes remain precise cited inputs.
The CP2 pseudoholomorphic interpolation argument in section 5.4, including Gromov compactness and transversality, is cited through the slow-growth result rather than expanded as a full proof.
General contact-manifold elementary spectral invariants beyond Liouville boundaries are referenced, not independently reconstructed.
The section 7.1 alpha-strong closing problem and the Katok-type near-periodic examples are not expanded into separate branches.
Orbifold Gromov-Witten and SFT Assumption 1.3 is retained; no unconditional general Hofer near-periodic theorem is claimed.
High-dimensional modified-capacity results remain announcements because the report cites an in-preparation manuscript.

Almgren-Pitts compactness, interpolation, regularity, White bumpy-metric theory and Sharp compactness are cited. General min-max construction and higher-dimensional singular variants are not claimed proved locally.
Generic minimal-hypersurface equidistribution, Song's general infinitude theorem and the detailed two-dimensional width computation are not expanded.

reports.speaker: Joshua Zahl
reports.title: A Survey of the Kakeya Conjecture, 2000–2025
reports.question: 丰富方向的线段为何必须占据满维空间，多尺度非集中又如何控制其重叠？
reports.reading_scope: Read published §§1–4, including definitions, historical examples, three-dimensional proof outline, broad and narrow estimates; cross-checked arXiv v1. Reused existing projection and restriction branches rather than duplicating them.

proof_scope.2I0C: D(1), exponent convergence and the final volume implication proved; the two geometric improvement propositions are cited.
proof_scope.2I0J: Weighted transversality imposed only on a measurable region carrying a fixed positive fraction of the tube mass. The restricted Lq and Holder deduction is proved; the weighted multilinear input is cited.
proof_scope.2I0K: Full theorem cited; the disjoint counting model only explains the exponent.
proof_scope.2I07: Exact cardinality and containment proved over the dual-number ring; no plane nonconcentration theorem claimed.

deferred: Complete proof of the Wang–Zahl structure and strict-improvement propositions.
Full Bourgain discretized projection theorem and regulus-strip incidence arguments.
Endpoint multilinear Kakeya proof and polynomial partitioning broad/narrow induction.
Complete passage from shaded multiscale estimates to Hausdorff dimension; existing theorem retained with citation.

Otis Chodosh: The official section 6 displays -Delta_H2 >= -1/4. The useful sharp lower bound is +1/4, independently proved in 2G0D.
The hyperbolic-plane example supplies strict spectral positivity of -a Delta + K only for a > 4. At a = 4 its bottom is zero; no endpoint counterexample is asserted.
The source's instructions to pretend spectral positivity is pointwise positivity are explanatory shortcuts, not mathematical implications. 2G0C inserts the conformal step.
The stable closed-surface genus statement is given with orientability explicit; a two-sided nonorientable surface in a nonorientable ambient manifold requires separate treatment.
Scalar mean curvature uses A(X,Y)=<nabla_X nu,Y> and vector mean curvature uses -H nu. The normalization difference in the existing conformal-surface page is stated.
The hyperbolic page 0C81 uses the opposite Laplace sign; 2G0D explicitly fixes Delta=div grad.
The torical-band bound is strict; the stable Bernstein range is intrinsic dimension <= 5; generic regularity is ambient dimension <= 11.

Kei Irie.issue: Published HTML omits the factor a in c_k(X,a lambda).
Kei Irie.handling: 2H0K uses c_k(X,a lambda)=a c_k(X,lambda), as forced by action scaling.

Kei Irie.issue: Printed omega_k(M,a g)=a^(dim M-1) omega_k(M,g) is not the bilinear-metric scaling convention used in these notes.
Kei Irie.handling: 2H0Q proves omega_k(M,c g)=c^((m-1)/2) omega_k(M,g). Length scaling by a corresponds to tensor a^2 g. Independently checked against the n/2 metric-ratio exponent in Irie–Marques–Neves Lemma 2.1; no attribution of an unverified author convention.

Kei Irie.issue: Some ambient-chain and reference-cycle labels in the published formula are inconsistent.
Kei Irie.handling: Existing 140N relative-chain definition retained; ambiguous formula not copied.

Joshua Zahl: Both publisher and arXiv Conjecture 1.3-prime print an upper bound; 2I03 proves the intended lower-bound direction independently.
Publisher/arXiv shaded variants repeat union T instead of union Y(T). Local statements use the actual shaded union.
The published multilinear sums mix k and n indices. 2I0J consistently sums k-tuples and multiplies k indicators.
The narrow-case heuristic prints mu^(-2); the count delta^(-1)mu^2 times tube volume delta^3 yields delta^2mu^2, as checked in 2I0K.
Source fine-child count (delta/rho)^2 is reversed in one explanatory sentence; no such count is copied into the definition.

review.independent_review: Chodosh agent independently checked Zahl 2I01,03,04,05,06,07,0C,0D,0G,0H,0J,0K. Corrected the maximal-separated direction quantifier in 2I05 and made c0-dependence explicit in 2I0J. Parent read the new narratives, main variation/calibration proofs, strong-closing implications, spectrum branch, scaling and exponent arguments. Final refinement restricts transversality to a positive-mass region, so unshaded fringes need not be transverse; the restricted-norm deduction is explicit.
review.prerequisite_candidate_scope: New 2G/2H/2I entries reviewed. Added genuine first-use links. Quantitative transversality in the Kakeya notes is defined by determinants or Gram volumes locally; it is not automatically the differential-topological definition at 0F50.
review.terminology: Existing Chinese mathematical terminology reused. Banana Space was not independently accessible; no complete new terminology-site verification claimed.
